prerequisites: A degree with basic training in Mathematics and Physics

learning_outcomes.text: Identify the possibilities of energetic valorization of biomass according to its characteristics.
Interpret the legislation and regulations applicable to biomass and biofuels.
Determine fuel consumption, its cost, and CO2 emissions associated with an installation that uses biomass as fuel.

syllabus_topics: Overview of the biomass resource. Usage data and resource potential, geographical distribution
Analysis of biomass types. According to origin, possibilities, potential, characteristics
Biomass transformation processes: physical, thermochemical, and biological.

Introduction to transformation processes, Justification of processes based on biomass characteristics. Economic valuation of target products. Transformation possibilities, historical evolution of processes. First transformation processes.
Thermochemical processes: General description and characteristics of suitable products for this process.

Combustion. Differences between biomass combustion and conventional fuels. Mass combustion. Types of grate. Semi-suspension combustion, suspension combustion. Screw burners, cyclonic burners, drum burners.
Combustion systems applied to small-scale heat generation. Heating boilers. Transformation of raw material to adapt it to small-scale systems.
Combustion systems applied to large-scale heat generation, steam and electricity production, cogeneration, trigeneration, and polygeneration.
Fluidized bed combustion 1. Types of fluidized beds, general characteristics. Description of a fluidized bed boiler.
Case study 1. Standard 50MW thermal power plant.
Gasification processes. Types of gasifiers. Applications of gas, fuels derived from syngas.
Biochemical processes. General characteristics of these processes. Anaerobic processes for methane production, biogas.
Biofuels. Biochemical processes applied to biofuel production. Bioalcohols and their derivatives
Characteristics of oil-based biofuels. Biodiesel. Production methods, most prominent characteristics.
assessment_rules: For students with continuous evaluation, if the written exam score (EX) is 3.5 or higher, the final grade is calculated as (0.1 x CT) + (0.1 x CP) + (0.2 x EC) + (0.6 x EX). If EX is below 3.5, the final grade is EX. For students with differentiated evaluation, if EX is 3.5 or higher, the final grade is (0.1 x CT) + (0.1 x CP) + (0.8 x EX). If EX is below 3.5, the final grade is EX. In both cases, a minimum course score of 5.0 is required to pass the subject. For extraordinary calls, the final grade for continuous evaluation students is (0.1 x CT) + (0.1 x CP) + (0.8 x EX) using ordinary call CT and CP scores, requiring a minimum EX of 3.5; otherwise, the grade is EX. The same rules apply to differentiated evaluation students in extraordinary calls. In case of doubt about authorship, students may be asked for an in-person defense.
